title: Sum of Largest Prime Substrings
summary: Given a string, identify the three largest unique prime numbers formed by any of its substrings.
statement: Given a string, identify the three largest unique prime numbers formed by any of its substrings. Sum these primes; if fewer than three exist, sum all found primes. Return 0 if no primes are found. Each prime is counted once, and leading zeros in substrings are disregarded.
constraints: Convert every nonempty substring to an integer, ignoring leading zeros.
Sum the three largest distinct primes, or every distinct prime when fewer than three exist.
hints: There are only O(n²) substrings, but repeated numeric values must be deduplicated before selecting the largest three.
Build each substring value incrementally and use deterministic Miller-Rabin to test primality efficiently.
For every start, append digits to a running value, add primes to a set, then sort the set and sum its last three entries.
Incremental construction enumerates every substring once; the set enforces uniqueness, and deterministic witnesses correctly classify all values allowed by the ten-digit limit.
editorial: Incremental construction enumerates every substring once; the set enforces uniqueness, and deterministic witnesses correctly classify all values allowed by the ten-digit limit.

tests.explanation: The distinct primes are 2, 3, 23, 223, and 1223; the largest three sum to 1469.
The only distinct prime substring value is 11.
